text:
alex: grabbed a perfetto trace from a noisy canary run — prefix cache reuse is terrible for short/interactive prompts. trace: https://perfetto.local/Ui/trace/1762554321 (nvtx markers present)

maya: link works. quick take: reuse looks ~10-15% in the heatmap? can you paste the aggregated numbers you ran locally?

alex: pasted raw perfetto SQL snapshot I ran:
```
-- perfetto sql (aggregated counters)
prefix_hits = 124
prefix_misses = 912
reuse_rate = 0.119
avg_batch_size = 1.8
kernel_launch_count = 1842
``` 
small note: most hits come from long-context requests; short prompts barely reuse cache.

chen: that reuse_rate aligns with what I saw. cache TTL + LRU eviction seems too aggressive for our request mix (many short-lived sessions). also observed a ton of tiny kernels in the timeline.

liam: timeline shows frequent tiny attention kernels (50us) with 4-10us gaps. overhead from kernel selection + launch dominates. suspect we pick a low-occupancy kernel variant for short sequences.

sophia: do we have an nsys capture for the same run? kernel timelines + CPU stack would help identify selection hotpath.

alex: yes - nsys saved at /tmp/run-1762554321.nsys. command I used:
```
nsys profile -o /tmp/run-1762554321 -t cuda,cudnn,osrt --capture-range=nvtx --force-overwrite -- ./serve_canary --config canary.json
```
NVTX ranges: BATCH_START / BATCH_END / KV_LOOKUP

maya: quick grep of the nsys stack shows a hot CPU function: kernel_selector::choose_variant (lots of samples). iterates over candidates per request.

chen: sounds like kernel selection doing per-request linear scan. maybe memoize based on (model, seq_len, device_properties) -> kernel id. small cache would avoid repeated work for identical shapes.

liam: agreed. also batching heuristic: current max-wait = 0ms for tail requests on hosted tier. bumping to 5ms on my local run increased avg_batch_size -> 4.1 and reuse_rate -> 0.42. perfetto snippet:
```
before: avg_batch_size=1.8 reuse=0.12 kernels/sec=520
after (5ms): avg_batch_size=4.1 reuse=0.42 kernels/sec=210
``` 
but p50 latency moved from 18ms -> 24ms for short prompts.

sophia: tradeoff note: latency vs cost. need canary and SLA gates. we should measure p90/p99.

alex: proposed action items:
- add microbench harness that simulates mixed prompt distribution (1-8 token short vs 32-512 long). record: prefix_hits/misses, avg_batch_size, kernel_count, p50/p90/p99. (owner: chen)
- add small memoization cache in kernel_selector keyed by (model_id, seq_len_bucket, device_caps) with TTL 30s (owner: liam)
- experiment: bump batching max-wait to 5ms on a 1% canary, capture nsys+perfetto and metrics (owner: alex)
- tweak prefix cache policy: increase per-model min-residency and use LFU bucket for very short sessions (owner: maya)

chen: I'll start on harness. quick repro sketch added to thread:
```
# repro microbench (py-like pseudocode)
for mix in [(0.8,0.2),(0.5,0.5)]:
  for i in range(2000):
    prompt_len = sample_short_or_long(mix)
    send_request(prompt_len)
    if i % 200 == 0: flush_metrics()
# capture nsys on the server and parse /metrics/prefix_stats.json
```

maya: perf-bot flagged anomaly yesterday: "prefix_miss_rate > 0.7 for model-x in prod" — attaching alert screenshot. we should emit prefix_hit_rate metric per route so we can SLO it.

liam: I'll open WIP PR: kernel-selector memo + small unit tests. will also add NVTX spans around selection. PR will include a config flag to enable memoization.

sophia: canary plan: enable batching-wait=5ms + enable memoization on 1% of hosts, gather nsys/perfetto + metrics for 24h, then decide.

alex: thanks team. next steps: chen starts harness today, liam PR for selector, maya for cache policy tweak proposal, I'll run canary and collect traces. ping me here with links to nsys/perfetto captures. :thumbsup:

perf-bot: scheduled nsys capture for canary run (id=run-1762554400) will upload to /artifacts/perf/run-1762554400.nsys when complete.

maya: one more data point — perfetto stack graph shows 35% of CPU samples in http_dispatcher waiting on lock around cache access. might need to reduce locking in KV lookups.

chen: noted. I'll make harness capture contented_lock_time metric too.

alex: great. saving the perfetto and nsys links in the canary issue: https://redwood/issues/ENG-PRF-523

liam: opened PR draft: https://github.com/redwood/inference/pull/987 (kernel-selector memo). comments welcome.

sophia: will coordinate canary rollout with infra. thanks all.
